title: A week in Washington, DC
summary: Seven days of free museums and monuments, half-smokes and Ethiopian dinners, Georgetown walks and cherry trees on the Tidal Basin.
author: friends of Placemoir

places.name: The Hay-Adams
places.notes: Across Lafayette Square from the White House. Ask for a room facing it, then have a drink in Off the Record downstairs.

places.name: The Jefferson
places.notes: A quiet, elegant 1923 hotel, with Jefferson's letters on the walls and a cozy bar.

places.name: Kimpton Hotel Monaco Washington DC
places.notes: A marble 1839 post office in Penn Quarter, steps from the Portrait Gallery and the Metro.

places.name: Hotel Hive
places.notes: Tiny, well-designed rooms near the Lincoln Memorial. The budget pick, with a rooftop bar.

places.name: Ben's Chili Bowl
places.notes: The chili half-smoke, served on U Street since 1958.

places.name: Old Ebbitt Grill
places.notes: The city's oldest saloon, a block from the White House. Go for oysters at the late-night happy hour.

places.name: Rasika
places.notes: Modern Indian cooking. The crispy spinach, palak chaat, is famous for a reason.

places.name: Zaytinya
places.notes: José Andrés's Greek, Turkish and Lebanese small plates in a bright, airy room.

places.name: Le Diplomate
places.notes: A Paris brasserie on 14th Street. Book weekend brunch ahead.

places.name: Compass Rose
places.notes: Street food from around the world in a cozy rowhouse. Order the khachapuri.

places.name: Founding Farmers
places.notes: Big, comforting American plates from a restaurant owned by farmers. Good for breakfast.

places.name: Martin's Tavern
places.notes: A Georgetown tavern since 1933, where JFK is said to have proposed to Jackie in booth three.

places.name: Union Market
places.notes: A food hall in an old wholesale market. Graze a little from everywhere.

places.name: Eastern Market
places.notes: A market hall since 1873. Get the blueberry buckwheat pancakes at the Market Lunch counter on a weekend.

places.name: Call Your Mother
places.notes: A Jew-ish deli with bagels people line up for. The Georgetown shop is a tiny pink house.

places.name: Baked & Wired
places.address: 1052 Thomas Jefferson St NW, Washington, DC 20007
places.notes: Cupcakes and coffee by the C&O Canal, a calmer pick than the famous cupcake line nearby.

places.name: Kramers
places.notes: An independent bookstore with a cafe and bar at the back, open late.

places.name: Round Robin Bar
places.notes: The Willard hotel's round bar, where Henry Clay mixed his first mint julep in Washington.

places.name: Lincoln Memorial
places.address: 2 Lincoln Memorial Cir NW, Washington, DC 20002
places.notes: Go at night, when it's lit and quiet, and read the Gettysburg Address on the wall.

places.name: Washington Monument
places.notes: Free timed tickets to the top. Reserve online a day or two ahead.

places.name: United States Capitol
places.notes: Free tours from the visitor center. Book ahead, and add the galleries through your representative.

places.name: Library of Congress
places.notes: The Jefferson Building's Great Hall is breathtaking. Take the tunnel from the Capitol.

places.name: The White House
places.notes: See it from Lafayette Square or the Ellipse. Tours are requested through your member of Congress.

places.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
places.notes: Start at the bottom, in the history galleries, and work your way up. Allow most of a day.

places.name: National Air and Space Museum
places.notes: The Wright Flyer, Apollo 11 and the Spirit of St. Louis. Free, with timed passes.

places.name: National Museum of Natural History
places.address: 10th St NW & Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC 20560
places.notes: The Hope Diamond, the dinosaur hall and the giant squid. Free.

places.name: National Gallery of Art
places.notes: The only Leonardo in the Americas, and a sculpture garden with an ice rink in winter.

places.name: National Portrait Gallery
places.address: 8th St NW & F St NW, Washington, DC 20001
places.notes: The presidents, including the Obama portraits, and a glass-roofed courtyard to rest in.

places.name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
places.address: 100 Raoul Wallenberg Pl SW, Washington, DC 20024
places.notes: Powerful and hard. Free timed passes are needed from March to August.

places.name: Ford's Theatre
places.notes: Where Lincoln was shot in 1865, still a working theater, with the Petersen House across the street.

places.name: Washington National Cathedral
places.notes: Gothic arches, a Darth Vader gargoyle and views from the tower. Look for the moon rock in the space window.

places.name: Arlington National Cemetery
places.notes: The Kennedy graves and the changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

places.name: National Mall
places.notes: Two miles from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial. Walk it end to end once, then use the Circulator.

places.name: Tidal Basin
places.notes: The cherry trees in early spring, and the Jefferson and MLK memorials all year. Rent a paddle boat.

places.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial
places.address: 1850 W Basin Dr SW, Washington, DC 20024
places.notes: Dr. King carved from a Stone of Hope, with his words along the wall behind.

places.name: United States Botanic Garden
places.notes: A free glasshouse jungle at the foot of the Capitol. Good on a rainy or cold day.

places.name: Georgetown Waterfront Park
places.notes: Fountains and river views, with kayaks for rent at Key Bridge Boathouse.

places.name: Dumbarton Oaks
places.notes: Terraced gardens behind a Georgetown mansion. Best in spring.

places.name: Rock Creek Park
places.notes: Woods and trails right in the city. On weekends Beach Drive is closed to cars.

places.name: Theodore Roosevelt Island
places.notes: A wooded island in the Potomac with an easy loop trail and a statue of Teddy Roosevelt.
